english.title: Aid / abet / assist in selling, exposing, uttering, using stamp fraudulently produced by means of a genuine die
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowingly aided, abetted or assisted **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) to knowingly

(A)_[sell]_
(B)_[expose for sale]_
(C)_[utter or use]_

a stamp which had been fraudulently produced by means of a genuine die
english.legislation: Contrary to section 13(1), (2) and (8) of the Stamp Duties Management Act 1891.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowingly aided / abetted / assisted in
selling/exposing for sale / uttering / using a stamp
which had been fraudulently produced
by means of a genuine die

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) The wording of section 13, and the definition of 'die', 'stamp' and 'stamped' in section 27, were amended on 22nd April 2019 to include stamps made by any machine, not just impressed stamps. For offences prior to this date, see offence document H.

other.penalty:
Either Way -

Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
